subject: Post-call: Hosted API capacity & unit-econ follow-up (monthly tokens + peak TPS)
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Priya Banerjee <priya@acuitylabs.com>, Amit Rao <amit@acuitylabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:30:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + request: monthly token volume & peak TPS

Hi Priya / Amit — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and the small asks so we can put together a matched hosted pricing model and an estimate for $/1M tokens.

Call summary (very short):
- Acuity is building a customer support assistant (multi-lingual) + a routing layer for triage.
- Current plan: 3 pilot customers in Q1, GA mid-2027.
- Primary model usage will be <generation> chat completions (average context ~1.2k tokens, synth responses ~300 tokens).

What we need from you to finalize a hosted estimate:
1) Expected monthly token volume range (low / likely / high) — include both input + output tokens if you can.
2) Peak TPS (inference requests per second) or concurrent sessions during peak minute.
3) Typical request profile: median and 95th percentile sequence lengths, and percent of requests that require streaming.
4) Target budget range for hosted inference (monthly) or a target $/1M tokens you’d like us to hit — helps us size discounts/reserved caps.

If easier, attach a sample traffic CSV with timestamped request counts (we can synthesize a load curve). I attached a short post-call notes PDF for your reference.

Next steps from our side: Marissa will prepare an initial hosted pricing estimate and a short options table (on-demand vs reserved commit) once we have the numbers above. Karthik may follow up on latency SLOs to validate kernel/quantization options.

Thanks — if you can send numbers by Monday 11/23 that would keep this on schedule for a pricing proposal next week.

Best,

Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment(s): post-call-notes-acuity-20261120.pdf (pdf)

From: Priya Banerjee <priya@acuitylabs.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: Amit Rao <amit@acuitylabs.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + request: monthly token volume & peak TPS

Hi Sergio — thanks for the clear summary. Agree with your notes. See answers below and attached sample traffic export.

Answers:
- Monthly token volume (expected):
  • Low: 40M tokens/mo (pilot)
  • Likely: 220M tokens/mo (post-first quarter ramp)
  • High: 1.1B tokens/mo (full rollout across 3 customers + partner integrations)
- Peak: our current estimate is ~95 TPS sustained for ~10 mins during peak support hours; short bursts to ~250 TPS for <60s when scheduled jobs hit.
- Request profile: median ≈ 900 tokens total (input+output), 95th ≈ 2,100 tokens; ~22% requests use streaming.
- Target budget: ideally <$1,800 per 1M tokens at scale; for pilot we can tolerate higher if there is a clear path to that rate with reserved capacity.

Attached: acuity_token_profile.csv with timestamped request counts and a column for avg total tokens per minute. Let us know if you need sample prompts or more granular P95 numbers.

—Priya
Priya Banerjee
Head of Product, Acuity Labs
priya@acuitylabs.com
Attachment(s): acuity_token_profile.csv (csv)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Banerjee <priya@acuitylabs.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + request: monthly token volume & peak TPS

Thanks Priya — that traffic sample is very helpful. A couple of quick clarifying questions from an infra/latency angle: 
1) What latency SLO do you need for the assistant? (p50/p95 targets). If you need p95 < 400ms we’ll prefer lower-batch/low-quantization runtime paths.
2) For the burst to 250 TPS, is that evenly distributed across короткие requests (low token count) or a mix? Bursty long-seq requests change GPU packing and can increase cost.

If you prefer, we can run a short synthetic run (we’ll need your sample prompts) and return estimated tokens/sec and expected $/1M tokens under three configurations (on-demand, reserved, and reserved + KV-caching).

Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Priya Banerjee <priya@acuitylabs.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted pricing options — preliminary economics and ask

Priya — looping in a very short pricing sketch while we wait on the latency SLO and any sample prompts. This is a ballpark to set expectations, not a final offer.

Sketch (estimated $/1M tokens at scale with reserved commit):
- Option A (conservative): $2,300 per 1M tokens — no KV caching, standard batching
- Option B (balanced): $1,650 per 1M tokens — reserved commit + automated prefix/KV caching
- Option C (aggressive): $1,250 per 1M tokens — larger commit, optimized quantized runtime (model permitting)

Observations:
- Given your target of <$1,800, Option B is achievable with a 6–12 month reserved commit around the "likely" volume (≈220M/mo) and some caching on user history.
- For the burst profile you described, we recommend reserving a small committed TPS buffer and enabling burst to handle the 250 TPS short spikes. That reduces on-demand premium costs.

Next steps:
1) Karthik: confirm latency/seq-length constraints (still pending).
2) Priya/Amit: confirm whether the "likely" monthly volume (220M) is the working baseline we should price against, or if you want a multi-tier commit table.
3) Sergio/Marissa: we’ll draft a simple committed-tier term sheet + example invoice showing projected monthly costs under each option — target delivery EOD Thu 11/26.

Thanks — happy to jump on a follow-up 30 min call if you want to walk through the options.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
Attachment(s): redwood_pricing_model_v2.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Priya Banerjee <priya@acuitylabs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted pricing options — preliminary economics and ask

All — thanks, this is very helpful. Confirming: use 220M tokens/mo as the baseline for the pricing table and include a row for the high-case (1.1B) so procurement can see scale economics.

Latency SLO: target p95 <= 750ms for the initial pilots (we can tighten later). Bursts include a mix of short and long requests; the 250 TPS spike is mostly short requests (under 600 tokens) triggered by scheduled syncs.

We’ll also share a sample of 50 prompts (anonymized) by EOD today for Karthik to run a quick synthetic. Looking forward to the term-sheet.

—Priya
